title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 launched 28 Sep — about 30% faster and up to 30% cheaper for most work than Sonnet 5
bullets.summary: Anthropic's new mid-tier model is pitched as the cheap-and-fast option rather than the smartest; the newsroom also lists Opus 5.5 (22 Sep) matching Fable 5.1 at ~40% lower cost.
bullets.how: The Construct: route high-volume scheduled jobs (daily scans, triage, drafting) to Sonnet 5.5 and keep Opus for hard reasoning; re-check API changes before switching model IDs. Brand 9 Signs/PRAGMA: lower per-task cost improves margins on agent work.

bullets.title: OpenAI launches 'dots' — always-on goal-driven agents on GPT-6 Astra (29 Sep, DevDay)
bullets.summary: Dots work continuously toward user-defined goals across 4,000+ apps incl. Slack and Teams; Pro/Business Premium first, Enterprise needs admin approval, UK/EU excluded at launch.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: direct competitor framing for 'always-on operator' offers — position on owned orchestration, governance and vertical know-how rather than the agent runtime. The Construct: benchmark against our launchd/Cowork scheduled jobs.

bullets.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 'Argon' (30 Sep), limited to trusted cyber defenders for now
bullets.summary: Google claims state-of-the-art coding and knowledge results, beating OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on several measures; pricing undisclosed and broader rollout (paying subscribers first) comes after more testing.
bullets.how: The Construct: nothing to wire yet — watch for general availability and pricing before benchmarking against Claude for coding/long-running agents.

bullets.title: Instinct raises $1B at a $10B valuation (Sequoia, Benchmark, Coatue)
bullets.summary: Independent enterprise AI-agent startup's round lands the same week OpenAI ships dots; investors are betting enterprises pay recurring revenue for agents, not just pilots.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: validates the market for agent operators and shows incumbents/startups crowding the space — differentiate on SMB/vertical delivery. Brand 9 Signs: no direct fit.

bullets.title: arXiv 2609.01736: Harness Engineering in LLM Tool Use via Agent-Native Reusable Tool Primitives
bullets.summary: Paper argues for building agents on reusable, agent-native tool primitives instead of ad-hoc per-task tool glue.
bullets.how: The Construct: matches our skills/MCP registry approach — consolidate repeated scripts (render checks, publish loops, scans) into shared primitives that every agent calls.

praxis_lesson: OpenAI, Google and a $1B-funded startup all pushed agents this week, so the runtime is commoditizing fast. The Construct's durable edge is the layer we own — reusable tool primitives, governance and vertical knowledge — and the model underneath should be swappable (e.g. Sonnet 5.5 for volume work).
